1000 SCFM of natural gas is about 1607 Nm³/h. This assumes the US gas-industry standard of 60 °F and 14.696 psia, and the usual normal conditions of 0 °C and 101.325 kPa.

Calculation (ideal gas, computed):
- 1000 ft³/min × 60 min/h × 0.0283168 m³/ft³ = 1699.0 m³/h at 60 °F
- × (273.15 K / 288.706 K) = 1607.5 Nm³/h

The result depends on which "standard" the SCFM uses. All values below were computed the same way:

| SCFM reference | Nm³/h |
|---|---|
| 60 °F, 14.696 psia | 1607.5 |
| 60 °F, 14.73 psia (AGA/US gas contracts) | 1611.2 |
| 68 °F, 14.696 psia | 1583.1 |
| 70 °F, 14.7 psia | 1577.6 |

These are ideal-gas numbers. I did not apply a compressibility correction. My expectation, not checked, is that natural gas is near-ideal at both reference states (Z about 0.998), so the result would change by well under 0.1%. No files were created.
